## Purpose and package topology
OpenUI is a pnpm TypeScript monorepo for a renderer-agnostic, streaming-first language that lets LLMs emit constrained UI trees. Core distribution targets are framework-neutral parsing/runtime, React/Vue/Svelte renderers, chat UI, agent adapters, CLI scaffolding, and observability. Workspace definition and package release surface: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `package.json`, `packages/`.

## Primary generation-to-render pipeline
1. A component library defines allowed UI components and typed contracts.
2. Prompt generation derives model instructions from that library.
3. An LLM or agent streams OpenUI Lang.
4. The parser incrementally produces/validates an AST and materializes it against the library.
5. Runtime evaluation resolves reactive state, expressions, queries, and tools.
6. Framework renderers turn the evaluated tree into live UI.
The framework-agnostic boundary is `packages/lang-core/src/library.ts`, `packages/lang-core/src/parser/`, and `packages/lang-core/src/runtime/`.

## Language core: parser, validation, and runtime
`@openuidev/lang-core` owns the canonical language semantics and has no UI-framework dependency. Lexer/parser/AST and serialization live in `packages/lang-core/src/parser/lexer.ts`, `packages/lang-core/src/parser/parser.ts`, and `packages/lang-core/src/parser/ast.ts`. Materialization and library validation enforce that generated components and props conform to registered contracts: `packages/lang-core/src/parser/materialize.ts`, `packages/lang-core/src/parser/validate-library.ts`. Runtime evaluates trees and properties, maintains state, and mediates queries/tools/MCP: `packages/lang-core/src/runtime/evaluate-tree.ts`, `packages/lang-core/src/runtime/store.ts`, `packages/lang-core/src/runtime/mcp.ts`.

## Rendering and component libraries
React bindings expose library definition, prompt publishing, streaming-aware rendering, state hooks, and runtime integration through `packages/react-lang/src/Renderer.tsx`, `packages/react-lang/src/library.ts`, and `packages/react-lang/src/runtime/reactive.ts`. Vue and Svelte are parallel renderer adapters built atop core concepts: `packages/vue-lang/src/Renderer.vue`, `packages/svelte-lang/src/lib/Renderer.svelte`. The React UI package supplies both primitive components and model-facing schemas/libraries; the bridge from generated names/props to React implementations is centered in `packages/react-ui/src/genui-lib/openuiLibrary.tsx`, `packages/react-ui/src/genui-lib/openuiChatLibrary.tsx`, and `packages/react-ui/src/genui-lib/index.ts`.

## Chat state and agent-stream boundary
`@openuidev/react-headless` separates chat state/artifacts/thread UI concerns from visual presentation. Its provider/stores manage messages, artifacts, detailed views, and tool activity: `packages/react-headless/src/store/ChatProvider.tsx`, `packages/react-headless/src/store/createChatStore.ts`, `packages/react-headless/src/store/artifactAutoOpenWatcher.ts`. Streaming adapters normalize AG-UI, LangGraph, Vercel AI SDK, OpenAI completions/responses, and Eve into shared message processing: `packages/react-headless/src/stream/adapters/index.ts`, `packages/react-headless/src/stream/processStreamedMessage.ts`. `packages/react-ui/src/components/AgentInterface/AgentInterface.tsx` and `packages/react-ui/src/components/OpenUIChat/` layer prebuilt React chat surfaces on that state.

## Integrations, operational tooling, and services
LangChain/LangGraph server integration transforms and relays agent streams via `packages/langchain/src/transformer.ts`, `packages/langchain/src/request-handler.ts`, and `packages/langchain/src/stream-relay.ts`. The CLI is the user-facing executable for app/example creation, generation, auth/key provisioning, and deployment; entry and major commands are `packages/openui-cli/src/index.ts`, `packages/openui-cli/src/commands/create-app.ts`, and `packages/openui-cli/src/commands/generate.ts`. Deployment includes a Vercel target (`packages/openui-cli/src/lib/deploy-targets/vercel/`). OpenUI Cloud-facing routes and client integration appear in `docs/app/api/openui-cloud/` and `docs/lib/openui-cloud/`; templates distinguish cloud and self-hosted startup paths under `templates/openui-cloud/` and `templates/openui-self-hosted/`.

## Documentation, examples, and telemetry
The Next.js documentation site is a consumer/integration showcase with app/API entrypoints in `docs/app/layout.tsx`, `docs/app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`, and `docs/app/api/playground/stream/route.ts`. Examples are independent reference apps across Next.js, FastAPI/Vite, React Native, Svelte, Nuxt/Vue, and agent frameworks, rooted at `examples/`. Observability has a vendor-neutral API plus a cloud transport pipeline with queueing/batching: `packages/observability/src/observability.ts`, `packages/observability-cloud/src/core/client.ts`, `packages/observability-cloud/src/core/transport.ts`.
